voice.instructions: Narrate an academic software demonstration for software engineering and information security researchers. Use a neutral, precise, measured tone with natural sentence pauses. Avoid promotional emphasis. Pronounce GadgetHunter as Gadget Hunter. Read LLM as the letters L L M, SMT as S M T, JSON as jay-sun, and FEASIBLE as the ordinary word feasible. Enunciate deserialization, satisfiability, and reachability clearly.

steps.label: Workflow overview
steps.say: GadgetHunter combines static taint analysis, LLM-assisted semantic reachability analysis, and SMT-based path feasibility checking for Java deserialization gadget chains.

steps.label: Target artifacts
steps.say: Upload the target application and its dependencies. This demonstration uses a Java test program compiled to bytecode.

steps.label: Candidate generation
steps.say: Set the search time limit and select automatic taint rules. Candidate generation uses static analysis and does not invoke an LLM.

steps.label: Coverage diagnostics
steps.say: Inspect the saved candidate-generation results and coverage diagnostics. Partial coverage does not rule out additional gadget chains.

steps.label: Candidate triage
steps.say: Review the ranked candidate clusters. Novel denotes no match to a catalogued gadget-chain family; it does not establish a new vulnerability.

steps.label: Source-level analysis
steps.say: Supply candidate chains and corresponding Java source code for region-based semantic reachability analysis and constraint extraction.

steps.label: Saved analysis report
steps.say: We now import a previously generated report for a separate, benign test case. No new source analysis is executed in this demonstration.

steps.label: Feasibility result
steps.say: FEASIBLE indicates satisfiability of the extracted constraints under the analysis model. It does not establish exploitability in the target environment.

steps.label: Call chain and constraints
steps.say: Inspect the call chain and extracted constraints to assess the data-flow relationships and path conditions represented by the analysis.

steps.label: Source inspection
steps.say: Examine the corresponding method implementation and the complete analysis record to review the basis for the reported result.

steps.label: Report export
steps.say: Export the analysis report as JSON to support manual review, independent validation, and subsequent analysis.
